subject: Re: Acme Health - model fit & streaming UX follow-ups
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Initial discovery - streaming QA for patient summarization

Thanks for the demo today, Marissa - really helpful. A couple quick follow-ups from our side:

- We need lower-latency partial responses in the UI so clinicians can see interim summaries while notes are still generating. Current prototype blocks until entire summary completes.
- We've seen some partial-output coherence issues: sometimes the streaming chunks repeat phrases or stop mid-sentence.
- Stop sequences are tricky - when a patient note includes abbreviations like "SOB" we want the model to not prematurely terminate.

Can you share recommended models and any benchmark links or prompt sets you used in the demo? Also interested in quantization options if that helps meet latency budgets.

Alex
Product Manager, Acme Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial discovery - streaming QA for patient summarization

Thanks Alex - great meeting. Recap and next steps below.

Recap:
- Goal: real-time streaming of clinical note summaries with <500ms per-chunk latency for interactive UX; final latency budget ~2s total for ~150 token summaries.
- Concerns: partial-output coherence, stop-sequence false positives on medical abbreviations, and occasional hallucinated steps in instructions.

Immediate next steps (owner):
1) We'll run a targeted eval on your sample prompt set and representative notes (Jordan).
2) Share model recommendations + quantization tradeoffs (me).
3) Quick engineering checklist for stop-sequence handling and client-side reassembly (Jordan + Rishi).

Attachments: prompt-set-v1.jsonl (your sample prompts + edge-cases) - thanks for sending.

I recommend we try two model variants for an initial A/B:
- redwood/clarity-7b (int8, baseline) - good coherence, lower memory footprint
- redwood/clarity-13b (q4_0) - better instruction-following for medical language, slightly higher latency but fewer hallucinations

Benchmark link: https://redwood-inference.internal/evals/ACME-1143/benchmark-results (will add numeric table after Jordan runs the job).

I'll have Jordan run evls on the exact prompt set and return timing/coherence metrics by Fri 13 Nov.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec - Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial discovery - streaming QA for patient summarization

Hi Alex - I ran the eval on your prompt-set-v1.jsonl against the two model variants Marissa suggested. High-level results attached (acme_health_model_eval_results.pdf) and quick notes below.

Findings:
- Clarity-7b (int8): median chunk latency 320ms, 95th percentile 580ms on our standard xPU (p3-like). Coherence metric: 82% (measured by overlap + human pass/fail on 200 samples).
- Clarity-13b (q4_0): median chunk latency 520ms, 95th percentile 900ms. Coherence metric: 92% with fewer stop-sequence false positives.

Streaming UX observations:
- Partial-output repetition often occurs when the client resends a tokenized prefix or when the server flushes small KV-cache windows. We recommend enabling prefix deduplication on the client and the server-side continuous-kv caching setting in our runtime (see checklist).
- Stop-sequence false positives correlate with presence of short uppercase tokens (SOB, HR, BP). Tunable strategy: prioritize token-level stop detectors but whitelist common medical abbreviations in the stop-token detector.
- For latency: if you must hit <300ms median, we can use the 7b int8 with aggressive batching and client-side incremental rendering. For better quality at ~500ms, 13b q4_0 is the sweet spot.

Next actions:
- Rishi: share engineering checklist for stop-sequence handling and recommended client changes.
- Alex: confirm target latency SLO (median and p95) and the sample traffic pattern (tokens/sec, concurrent users).

Jordan
Applied ML Engineer - Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial discovery - streaming QA for patient summarization

Alex, quick technical checklist for your frontend/backend teams to reduce partial coherence and stop issues:

1) Client-side:
- Implement prefix-deduplication: when app receives chunk N, do not resend the last 3 tokens as a new request.
- Render incremental chunks but suppress UI if chunk confidence < threshold (we surface confidence in the streaming metadata).
- Add a local whitelist of common medical abbreviations (SOB, HR, BP, RR) to avoid treating them as stop sequences.

2) Server-side/runtime config (Redwood):
- Enable continuous-kv-cache with window=1024 and flush=auto - reduces repetition on long context.
- Use token-level stop detector with abbreviation whitelist.
- For latency SLOs: prefer redwood/clarity-7b int8 + dynamic batching; if you need higher quality, redwood/clarity-13b q4_0 with tail-latency-aware routing.

3) Telemetry & monitoring:
- Add per-chunk coherence metric (string overlap) and stop-trigger counts to the App Dashboard.
- Alert if p95 chunk latency > target or stop-trigger rate spikes >2% of requests.

I can pair with your infra engineer for a 30-min runbook review this week. What windows work for you?

Rishi
Senior Backend Engineer - Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial discovery - streaming QA for patient summarization

Thanks team - this is super helpful. Quick answers and next steps:

- Target SLOs: median chunk latency <= 350ms, p95 <= 800ms. We're okay with occasional higher p95 during batch imports but want interactive sessions to stay within the SLO.
- Traffic profile: peak 120 concurrent clinicians, average 40, each generates ~3 streaming sessions/hour with ~150 tokens per session.
- We'd like to pilot Clarity-13b q4_0 for a week on a canary subset (10% traffic) and fall back to Clarity-7b int8 if we see regression.

Can you confirm pricing delta for the 13b canary and a rough timeline for the checklist pairing session? Also please upload the full eval csv to the Drive link when available.

Alex
Product Manager, Acme Health
